newsitem.title: INDIA: India to up incentives for private road builders.
newsitem.headline: India to up incentives for private road builders.

text.p: India plans to extend tax reliefs on private road projects to 20 years from 12 to make them more attractive to entrepreneurs, a senior government official said on Wednesday.
"We are talking with the government to enhance tax holiday from 12 years to 20 years," A.D. Narain, director-general (roads) of the federal ministry of surface transport, said.
Private road projects now enjoy a five-year tax holiday and a concessional tax rate for another five years. The concession is to be availed of within 12 years of beginning of operations.
"We are also signing MoU (memorandum of understanding) with state governments on exploitation of land for sweetening some projects," Narain told an infrastructure seminar.
But he said commercial exploitation of land around a road presented lot of issues yet to be resolved. Could such income be treated as income from infastructure, he asked.
Narain said the state-run National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) would form joint ventures with private parties.
The government planned to convert the existing two-lane roads into four-lanes with private participation, he added.

The following are the major projects identified for private investment -- widening from two lanes to four lanes (4,000 km), 50 major bridges, 50 railway overbridges and 30 bypasses and 1,000 km of expressways.
India opened the road sector to private sector as part of its economic reforms launched in 1991.
The National Highways Act of 1956 was amended in June 1995 to permit private sector participation.
